propositions: When an ordered pair holds two differently-related net-active dependencies (e.g., blocks and relates_to), pair-scoped removal via rebar.unlink cannot converge because it targets only the most-recent relation, leaving the older one to trigger a permanent G5 decline loop on inbound peer deletions.

The write path (add_dependency) is relation-scoped keyed on (target_id, relation), but the removal path (_get_link_info) is pair-scoped with no relation parameter, creating an API asymmetry that prevents removal of a specific relation from a double-related pair.

When a peer deletes one relation from a double-related pair, the inbound removal record survives G4 deduplication and reaches G5 mismatch check, which declines permanently because the named relation differs from the pair's most-recent net-active relation, causing non-convergence without operator-visible signal beyond logging.

The fix makes removal symmetric with writes by adding a relation-scoped seam (graph_links.remove_dependency) and threading an optional relation parameter through the removal stack, while keeping rebar.unlink(id1, id2) backward-compatible by defaulting to pair-scoped most-recent behavior when no relation is specified.
A removal naming a relation with no matching net-active local link must remove nothing and log as a no-op, preserving the safety invariant that no link the peer still carries is ever removed.

The reconciler's inbound removal path (apply_inbound_records._inbound_unlink_one) must use relation-scoped removal so that G5 mismatch cases converge by removing exactly the mirrored relation instead of declining forever.
